title: What the SDKs send and receive for ZPA Microtenants

prose.text: This subject records what the SDKs send and receive for Microtenant objects beyond the field list: dropped zero values, response handling and the two search styles. The product behavior is in [[zpa.microtenants.lifecycle]], [[zpa.microtenants.api-scoping]] and [[zpa.microtenants.share-and-move]].
{{post-search-query-and-page}} The body shape differs from the specification {{divergence:search-body-shape}}, and so does the operator vocabulary {{divergence:search-operator-vocabulary}}.
Priority has different types in the contract and Go {{divergence:priority-type}}.
Whether the string form is accepted is open {{gap:priority-string-accepted}}.
A microtenant read through Python does not expose roles, the admin user or priority: {{python-model-attributes}}
The enabled default differs between the Python docstring, the Python write path and Go {{divergence:enabled-default-sources}}.

checks.do: Whether a microtenant update meant to disable it was sent with enabled false, which the Go struct always includes.
Whether an update through the Python SDK passed microtenant_id as a keyword argument as well as the positional id.
Whether a failed create with an AuthDomain criterion named a domain registered to the customer.
Whether a hand-built search body followed the specification or the Go SDK's nested shape.

enabled-tags.statement: The Go microtenant struct sends `enabled` and `privilegedApprovalsEnabled` without omitempty, so false is always on the wire, while the embedded user's `enabled` is omitempty and a false there is dropped. The Python model leaves enabled as None when the key is absent.

quotes: self.enabled = config["enabled"] if config and "enabled" in config else None

user-key-and-output-only.statement: The Go struct holds the admin user under the JSON key `user` and the roles under `roles`, both omitempty. The specification defines both in the microtenant GET and create responses.
user-key-and-output-only.conditions: The create and update request schemas in the specification list neither roles nor user (checked by reading both schemas); an absence cannot be pinned by a pointer.

criteria-attribute-authdomain.statement: The Go SDK's tests and the Python SDK's example set a microtenant's criteriaAttribute to `AuthDomain` with a domain in criteriaAttributeValues, and the Go test treats an error containing `domains.does.not.belong.to.customer` as the sign that the domain is not registered to the customer.

quotes: // Check for specific error message and continue if found

criteria-attribute-authdomain.conditions: No other criteriaAttribute value appears in the SDK sources read; whether the API accepts others is not shown, and neither SDK enforces a list.

summary-bare-array.statement: GET /microtenants/summary returns a bare array of id and name objects rather than the usual wrapper with a list; the Python SDK returns an empty list when the body is not a list. From v1.11.3 it returns that list as the first element of a (result, response, error) tuple; up to v1.11.2 it returned a 2-tuple.

evidence.note: the microtenant list itself is wrapped: list, totalPages, totalCount, currentCount

update-rebinds-id.statement: In the Python SDK's update_microtenant, the microtenant_id argument used to build the URL is reassigned from the request body's microtenant_id key (kept in the body) before the query parameter and the 204 stand-in object are built, so a caller who does not also pass microtenant_id as a keyword gets no microtenantId query parameter and a stand-in object whose id is None.

quotes: # Use get instead of pop to keep microtenant_id in the body
# Handle case where no content is returned (204 No Content)

update-rebinds-id.conditions: Read from the code at the pin; not executed.

update-returns-204.statement: PUT on a microtenant returns 204 No Content in the specification, and the Go SDK's Update decodes no response body (it passes nil as the response target) and its signature returns an `*http.Response` and an error, not a microtenant.

get-by-name-two-paths.statement: The Go microtenants package has two name lookups. GetByName lists with GET using the name as the search text and matches case-insensitively on the client; GetMicrotenantByName posts a name-equals search to /microtenants/search with the service's microtenant as a query parameter and matches case-insensitively on the client.

search-body-shape.summary: The shape of the POST /microtenants/search body: the specification and the Python docstring describe filterBy as a flat array of filter objects with values, while the Go SDK sends a nested filterGroups structure with a single value.

positions.says: The Python get_microtenant_search docstring documents filter_by as a flat list of filter objects, each with filter_name, operator and a values list.

quotes: - **filter_by** (list): A list of filter condition dictionaries.
- **values** (list): A list of values to match.

positions.says: The specification defines filterBy as an array of items with filterName, operator, values and commaSepValues.
The Go request type nests filterGroups inside filterBy, each group holding filters with a single `value` key.

search-body-shape.impact: A raw search built from the specification will not match the body the Go SDK sends. The Go SDK's microtenant name lookup is the only evidence in these sources of a body that works, and its result was not observed here. See [[zpa.microtenants.api-scoping]].

search-operator-vocabulary.summary: The operator words for microtenant search filters: the Go SDK sends EQ, while the Python SDK's docstring shows EQUALS and LIKE.

positions.says: The Go microtenant name search hard-codes the operator EQ.

evidence.after: func GetMicrotenantByName(ctx context.Context, service *zscaler.Service, microtenantName string) (*MicroTenant, *http.Response, error) {

positions.says: The Python get_microtenant_search docstring lists EQUALS and LIKE as example operators.

search-operator-vocabulary.impact: The specification types operator as a free string, so neither word is confirmed by it. Use the Go word EQ only as the one an SDK actually sends; a filter with EQUALS or LIKE has no sent-and-working example in these sources.

priority-type.summary: The OpenAPI document types a microtenant's `priority` as an int32 integer, while the Go SDK types it as a string.

positions.says: The contract microtenant list item has priority as an int32.
The Go MicroTenant struct declares Priority as a string.

priority-type.impact: The Go SDK sends a JSON string where the contract has a number; whether the API coerces or rejects it is not shown.

enabled-default-sources.summary: The Python microtenant docstring says `enabled` defaults to True, while the Python add_microtenant sends the caller's keyword arguments as the body unchanged and the Go struct always sends `enabled`.

positions.says: The Python add_microtenant docstring says enabled defaults to True.

quotes: enabled (bool): Whether the microtenant is enabled. Defaults to True.

positions.says: The Python add_microtenant builds the body from the caller's keyword arguments alone, so a caller that does not pass enabled sends no enabled key.
The Go struct tags enabled without omitempty, so an unset value is sent as false.

enabled-default-sources.impact: A Go caller that leaves Enabled unset creates a disabled microtenant, while a Python caller omits the key and gets the server default; the docstring's True is not an SDK default. The docstring's default against the console's is in [[zpa.microtenants.lifecycle:enabled-default]].

priority-string-accepted.title: Whether the API accepts a string priority on a microtenant write
priority-string-accepted.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the Go SDK sends priority as a JSON string while the contract expects an integer, and it is unresolved whether the API coerces or rejects the string. Create a microtenant with a priority through the Go SDK in a scratch tenant and read it back.
priority-string-accepted.blocks: telling whether Go microtenant writes with a priority succeed
